newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle bid $63, offered $66-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle bid $63, offered $66-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle bids early Tuesday at $63.00 were passed by owners pricing cattle at $65.00 to $66.00, feedlot sources said.
Packer inquiry was strong, but sales were not expected to occur until Wednesday as owners wait to see how cattle futures react to Friday's USDA Cattle on Feed report, sources said.
The report showed January feedlot placements in the seven key states at 125 percent of a year ago, which greatly exceeded trade estimates.
Many feedlots reportedly remained current after last week's heavy sales volume.
The current status of feedlot marketings, coupled with firm beef demand were expected to offset potential weakness from last week's USDA monthly cattle data, some cattle feeders said.

Cash cattle prices this week were expected steady to $1.00 higher than last week's top of $64.00. Strength was expected from ideas that many of the cattle sold at midweek last week have already being delivered and slaughtered, they said.
Beef prices on Monday were quoted up $0.21 to $0.94 per cwt on 145 fabricated loads sold, USDA said.
